hooks.name: Auto-commit after each top-level spec task
hooks.description: After a top-level spec task completes, commits the task's files with a short Conventional Commits message. Never pushes. Uses credits (agent action).

action.prompt:
A spec task was just marked completed. Only act if a top-level task (an ID with no dot, like '3') is now completed, either directly or because its last subtask finished. If only a subtask completed and its parent is still open, do nothing.

Otherwise, commit without asking:
1. Run `git status --short -uall` to see what changed.
2. Stage by name only the files this task created or changed, plus the spec's tasks.md and tasks.meta.json. Never stage .env or anything gitignored. Leave unrelated changes unstaged.
3. Commit with a one-line subject: `<type>(<scope>): <summary>`, under 60 characters. Types: feat, fix, build, chore, test, docs, refactor. Scopes: backend, extension, graph, retailers, db, eval, kiro, docs. Add a body only if a decision isn't obvious from the diff, and keep it to one or two short lines. No file lists, no requirement IDs.
4. Print the commit hash and subject, then continue.

Never push, amend, or use --no-verify. If a pre-commit hook fails, report the error and stop.
